Subject: Billing boundary scenario — mixed short prompts vs long context (AtlasMedical)

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week — we had a few follow-ups from the engineering and procurement teams about how billing actually maps to our usage pattern. Quick summary of our traffic: most requests are short inference calls (~50–120 tokens) for classification, but roughly 10% of calls are long-document summarizations that keep a ~12k token context. We want to understand practical billing implications for a mixed pattern like that.

Specific asks:
- How are tokens attributed when a single session mixes short and long calls?
- Do long-context calls force a higher minimum (per-call or per-session)?
- How does rounding work across many short calls vs a few long calls in the same billing window?

Can you share a worked example with numbers and contract-friendly language we can show legal/procurement? I attached a spreadsheet with our sample volume.

Appreciate it — Jordan

Thanks Jordan — helpful context and good spreadsheet. High level answer up front: billing is token-based with two orthogonal mechanisms in play (per-request quantum/minimum and session-level context slabization) — you’ll want to confirm which contract applies (we can lock a long-context slab or meter per-token). Below I outline a couple of worked examples and recommended contract language for procurement. Sergio and Karthik are looping in for the math + SLA/terms language.

Summary bullets:
- Metering: we meter by tokens consumed (input + output) at the per-call level.
- Minimum/quantum: there is a per-request quantum that floors very short calls (e.g., 40 tokens), and a per-session slab option for long-context usage (you can commit to slab X for predictable unit pricing).
- Rounding: rounding occurs at the billing-window (monthly) aggregation after per-call floor application — we do not round up each tiny call if aggregated usage exceeds the quantum threshold back to the slab.

Worked example (your numbers, simplified):
- You do 90K short calls averaging 80 tokens (input+output) = 7.2M tokens.
- You do 6K long-context calls averaging 12k tokens = 72M tokens.
- If on pure per-token meter: total tokens = 79.2M tokens -> billed at per-token rate.
- If you purchase a 50k-token context slab (reserved capacity) for the long calls: long calls counted against slab allocations, short calls billed per-token; slab pricing usually gives ~40–60% discount on those long-context tokens.

Contract-friendly suggested language (short):
"Billing basis: Charges are computed on a per-token basis (input + output). A per-request minimum floor of N tokens applies to individual requests; Customers may optionally purchase reserved context slabs (SLAB_N tokens) that apply preferential pricing to tokens consumed within slab-qualified requests. Rounding is applied at the billing-window level after per-request floors are applied; fractional tokens are summed and billed at invoice time."

Next steps: Sergio will send a sample invoice calc and a short redline for procurement. Karthik will confirm the specific quantum used for your proposed pilot.

Best,

Jordan — quick note with concrete numbers and the sample calc attached. Apologies for the long table — I tried to keep it short.

Key numbers we typically use for pilots:
- Per-request minimum floor (quantum): 40 tokens. That means any single call will be billed as at least 40 tokens; calls above that are billed actual tokens (rounded to nearest integer token).
- Monthly billing-window rounding: we sum all tokens (after floor applied) for the invoice period and bill the total; no additional per-call rounding beyond the floor.
- Slab true-up: Reserved slabs are prepaid/committed. If you underutilize a committed slab, we offer a quarterly true-up credit against future consumption for mid-size commitments (negotiable in contract). For pilots under $X/month we typically offer a 30% utilization buffer credit in the first two months.

Sample numbers (based on your spreadsheet):
- Short calls: 90,000 calls * max(80, 40 floor) = 7,200,000 tokens billed.
- Long calls: 6,000 calls * 12,000 = 72,000,000 tokens.
- Pure per-token price (example): $0.00026 / token -> invoice = $20,592.
- Hybrid: buy 60M-token long-context slab at $0.00016/token (= $9,600 upfront) + remaining 19.2M tokens billed at $0.00026/token -> invoice roughly = $9,600 + $4,992 = $14,592 (plus terms).

Attachments: I included AtlasMed_billing_sample_calc.xlsx with both the per-token and hybrid worksheet and a short terms excerpt file (RDW-terms-digest-2026.pdf) you can share with legal.

Let us know if you want the slab size or discount adjusted — we can model a 40/50/60% slab discount and show the crossover point (tokens/month where slab starts saving money).

Cheers,
Sergio
